newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Woodside says Cossack to run full out.
newsitem.headline: Woodside says Cossack to run full out.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Wednesday it expects its offshore Cossack Pioneer crude oil facility to operate at full capacity in 1997.
The facility has been running at or above its rated capacity of around 115,000 barrels a day, but is earmarked to be partially shut down for maintenance work this year.

Production at Cossack is planned to be cut to 50,000 to 60,000 barrels of crude oil a day for three weeks, possibly in October, to allow repairs to be carried out on a faulty key component of the gas export system which is causing accelerated wear on other parts, the company said previously.

Woodside earlier on Wednesday posted a half-year net profit to June 30 of A$84.38 million, up from A$43.32 million in the corresponding period a year ago, and lifted its interim dividend to six cents from four cents.
Sales revenue of A$366.7 million for the latest half-year was up 27.1 percent from the corresponding period a year ago.
Domestic gas sales for the half-year rose 5.1 percent , owing to a slightly higher price and a drawdown in customers' inventories, Woodside said.
Considerable potential remains for further gas sales to new downstream projects in Australia, the company said.
It said The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's direct-reduced iron pellet plant under construction at Port Hedland, will be a major buyer of its gas starting next year.
The project will consume 130 terajoules of gas a day, with Woodside's share at 65 terajoules a day, the company said.
Results from its Perseus well have added to reserves of natural gas, making it possible to meet expanding demand for liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the North West Shelf project, the company said.
Last December, the Perseus-2 appraisal well encountered a 146-metre gas column, which lifted reserves.
A second discovery in April of another, smaller gas accumulation beneath the upper field, further enhanced reserves.
Eight Japanese LNG customers have signed a letter of indication confirming their desire to continue negotiations toward a major expansion of the Shelf project, Woodside said.
The expansion would see production of LNG double to around 14 million tonnes a year if a final agreement is reached, with additional LNG flowing by 2002, Woodside has said previously.
Equal partners in the North West Shelf are Woodside, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd and units of BHP, British Petroleum Co Plc, Chevron Corp and Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
